summary: ControlArena monitor prompt formatters embedded model-written tool-call arguments and chain-of-thought unsanitized, letting the monitored policy inject into the monitor prompt (ETB-02)
details:
ControlArena's monitor prompt formatters built the monitor prompt by interpolating untrusted model output with f-strings and str.format(). `control_arena/monitor/_last_tool_calls_prompt_formatter.py` and `_prefix_prompt_formatter.py` concatenated tool-call function names and arguments verbatim (reported as issue #791 on 2026-03-31), and `_cot_prompt_formatter.py` interpolated the monitored assistant message's content directly (reported as issue #809 on 2026-04-16). A policy under evaluation could therefore place text in a tool-call argument or in its chain of thought that the monitor reads as structural: fake section markers, directives, or a planted low suspicion score, biasing the monitor toward a low-suspicion verdict. This is ETB-02 (unsanitized model output in the evaluator prompt): the monitor's verdict depends on text the evaluated system writes.

The pages show formatter output and formatter tests. They do not show a monitor's verdict changing.

Fixes: pull request #798 (merged 2026-04-08, first released in control-arena 15.0.0) JSON-serializes tool-call arguments in both formatters and HTML-escapes the function name and the arguments inside the prefix formatter's existing `<tool_call_N>` tags. It carries the reporter's commit from pull request #795, which was closed as superseded, with formatting applied. Pull request #810 (merged 2026-04-30, first released in control-arena 16.0.0) wraps chain-of-thought content in `<cot>` tags, HTML-escapes it, and adds adversarial tests for closing-tag injection, newline-plus-fake-tag injection and format-specifier passthrough. Pull request #854, from another contributor (opened 2026-08-03, merged 2026-08-10, first released in control-arena 20.0.0 on 2026-10-05), found that the tool-call formatter still passed `<` and `>` from the function name and the arguments after #798, so a tool call could close the `<tool_calls>` block of the default monitor prompt. It HTML-escapes both fields. All three are breaking changes to monitor prompts, so monitor outputs produced before and after them are not directly comparable.

database_specific.note: 15.0.0 (2026-04-08) JSON-serialized tool-call arguments in the tool-call and prefix formatters and HTML-escaped the prefix formatter's fields (#798). 16.0.0 (2026-05-20) fixed the chain-of-thought formatter (#810). The tool-call formatter still passed angle brackets until 20.0.0 (2026-10-05, #854): git tag v19.0.0 does not contain that commit and tag v20.0.0 does (GitHub compare, 2026-11-13). 'introduced: 0' is a conservative bound; the first release containing the affected formatters is UNVERIFIED.

target.name: ControlArena
target.affected_component_versions: control-arena < 20.0.0. 15.0.0 fixed the prefix formatter and JSON-serialized tool-call arguments; 16.0.0 fixed the chain-of-thought formatter; 20.0.0 escaped angle brackets in the tool-call formatter

attack.description: The monitored policy emits a tool-call argument or chain-of-thought string containing text shaped like the monitor prompt's own structure (closing tags, section headers, instructions, or a stated suspicion score). The formatter interpolates it unescaped, so the monitor model reads attacker text as harness text and can be steered to a low suspicion score.
attack.preconditions: The policy under evaluation controls tool-call arguments or its visible reasoning; the monitor uses a markdown-based prompt formatter (default configuration). The effect on a monitor's suspicion score was not measured on the pages.
attack.poc_pointer: Adversarial test cases added in control-arena #798, #810 and #854 (TestLastToolCallsAdversarialInputs, TestPrefixAdversarialInputs and TestCotAdversarialInputs). They test formatter output.

hardening.fix: Wrap every model-derived field in delimited tags and HTML-escape it before it enters the monitor prompt; keep instructions in a role the policy cannot write; add adversarial formatter tests.
hardening.pattern: Escape or structurally neutralize model output before it enters any grader prompt; use message-role separation (taxonomy ETB-02 fix pattern).
hardening.residual_risk: Escaping prevents structural confusion but not persuasion: a monitor can still be argued with inside a correctly delimited block. Measure with the dynamic attacker strategy prompt_boundary_break.

disclosure.tier_reason: Public artifact, no non-public information, impact limited to the monitor's verdict, fix proposed with the report.
disclosure.released: control-arena 15.0.0, 16.0.0 and 20.0.0 (one part of the fix each)
disclosure.notes: The maintainer replied to issue #791 on the day it was filed and welcomed a pull request. The reporter opened pull request #795 on 2026-04-05. The maintainer opened #798 to carry that commit with ruff formatting applied and a breaking-change note, closed #795 as superseded and merged #798 on 2026-04-08. The follow-up issue #809 was fixed by the reporter's pull request #810, which the maintainer approved on 2026-04-27 and merged on 2026-04-30. A third pull request, #854 from another contributor, was opened on 2026-08-03. It escapes angle brackets that the tool-call formatter still passed after #798. The maintainer approved and merged it on 2026-08-10. The fixed date is that merge.
